Original_Claim: Initial numerical values systematically influence subsequent judgments of uncertain quantities
Outcome: Confirmed - Many Labs 1 found d>1.0 across 36 sites, one of most robust effects
Notes: Effect size remained very large in replications

Original_Claim: Events that are easier to recall are judged as more frequent
Outcome: Confirmed - Many Labs 3 replicated but with smaller effect (d=0.09 vs d=0.82)
Notes: Replication effect much smaller than original

Original_Claim: People are risk-averse for gains and risk-seeking for losses
Sample_Design: Lab experiments, N=152 in original, hypothetical choices
Outcome: Confirmed - Many Labs 1 showed consistent effect across sites (p=0.37 for heterogeneity)

Original_Claim: Color word interference significantly delays color naming responses
Sample_Design: Lab experiments, N=varied, within-subjects, very controlled
Outcome: Confirmed - Many Labs 3 found very large effect (d=2.04), serves as validity check
Notes: One of most robust effects in psychology

Original_Claim: Items at beginning (primacy) and end (recency) of lists are recalled better than middle items
Sample_Design: Lab experiments, N=varied, within-subjects, free recall paradigm
Outcome: Confirmed - Highly replicable across decades, basic memory phenomenon
Notes: Fundamental finding with clear neural correlates

Original_Claim: Semantically related primes facilitate lexical decision responses
Sample_Design: Lab experiments, N=varied, lexical decision task, within-subjects
Outcome: Confirmed - One of most robust findings in cognitive psychology, replicated hundreds of times
Notes: Considered foundational effect in word recognition

Original_Claim: Facial expressions can influence affective responses
Sample_Design: Lab experiments, N=92 original, pen-in-mouth paradigm
Outcome: Partial - RRR with 17 labs (N=4,493) found d=0.03 (CI: -0.11 to 0.16), failed to replicate
Notes: Failed in pen-in-mouth paradigm, but broader hypothesis may hold under different conditions

Original_Claim: A single exposure to American flag shifts support toward Republican beliefs
Sample_Design: Online study during 2008 election, N=varied, claimed 8-month duration
Outcome: Partial/Failed - Many Labs 1 did not replicate; authors later found time-varying effect
Notes: Original authors acknowledged effect declined to zero over time

Original_Claim: Sequential self-control tasks deplete a limited resource, impairing subsequent performance
Sample_Design: Lab experiments, N=varied, sequential task paradigm
Outcome: Failed - Multi-lab RRR (N=2,141) found d=0.04 (CI: -0.07 to 0.14); meta-analyses show publication bias
Notes: Multiple large replications found null effects

Original_Claim: Adopting expansive postures causes increases in testosterone, decreases in cortisol, and increased feelings of power
Sample_Design: Lab experiment, N=42, between-subjects, hormone measures
Outcome: Failed - Multiple replications failed to find hormonal effects; lead author Carney disavowed (2016)
Notes: Original effect likely due to small N, selective reporting

Original_Claim: Holding pen in teeth (smile) increases perceived humor compared to lips (pout)
Outcome: Failed - RRR with 17 labs (N=4,493) found d=0.03, none of 17 studies showed effect
Notes: Possible moderator: camera presence in replications

Original_Claim: Priming professor stereotype improves general knowledge performance compared to hooligan prime
Sample_Design: Lab experiment, N=varied, stereotype priming + trivia
Outcome: Failed - RRR with 40 labs (N=4,493) found 0.14% difference, no moderation by gender

Original_Claim: Exposure to elderly-related words causes participants to walk more slowly
Linguistic_Markers: causes participants to walk (definitive causal claim)
Sample_Design: Lab experiment, N=30, priming + walking speed measurement
Outcome: Failed - Doyen et al. (2012) with objective laser timing found d~0, discovered experimenter expectancy effects
Notes: Doyen showed effect reversed based on experimenter expectations

Original_Claim: Reminders of money increase self-sufficient behavior and decrease helping
Sample_Design: Lab experiments, N=varied across studies, multiple DVs
Outcome: Failed - Rohrer et al. (2015) found zero evidence across 4 large experiments; meta-analyses show selection bias
Notes: Meta-analytic tools indicate p-hacking and publication bias

Original_Claim: Threats to moral purity increase desire for physical cleansing products
Sample_Design: Lab experiments, N=varied, moral threat + cleansing product ratings
Outcome: Failed - Earp et al. (2014) failed 3 direct replications; meta-analysis of 15 studies found g=0.07 in independent labs
Notes: Macbeth Effect meta-analysis shows publication bias

Original_Claim: Recalling unethical behavior increases desire to cleanse oneself
Linguistic_Markers: increases desire (definitive causal claim, metaphorical link)
Sample_Design: Lab experiments, N=varied, recall task + hand-washing opportunity
Outcome: Failed - Multiple replication failures; meta-analysis found weighted g=0.17 overall, g=0.07 in independent labs
Notes: Effect appears to be publication bias artifact
